When Axios receives a URL with the data: scheme, its Node HTTP adapter decodes the entire payload into memory (as a Buffer or Blob) and returns a synthetic 200 response, completely bypassing the maxContentLength and maxBodyLength size limits that protect against oversized HTTP responses. This allows an attacker to supply an arbitrarily large data: URI and cause the Node.js process to exhaust memory and crash. Affected versions are Axios < 1.12.0 (1.x branch) and < 0.30.0 (0.x branch) for Node.js. The vulnerability was disclosed on September 11, 2025, and carries a CVSS v3.1 base score of 7.5 (High) (GitHub Advisory, Feedly). Technical details The root cause is CWE-770 (Allocation of Resources Without Limits or Throttling). In lib/adapters/http.js, when Axios detects a data: scheme URL, it calls fromDataURI() in lib/helpers/fromDataURI.js, which decodes the entire Base64 payload into a Buffer via Buffer.from(decodeURIComponent(body), 'base64') with no size checks. The maxContentLength and maxBodyLength guards only apply to HTTP stream responses and are entirely skipped for data: URIs — even when the caller explicitly sets responseType: 'stream' or configures size limits. An attacker who can supply a user-controlled URL to an Axios request (e.g., in a link-preview service or URL-fetching proxy that permits data: scheme) can trigger unbounded memory allocation. A public PoC is included in the official advisory, demonstrating a ~120 MB allocation that crashes a Node.js process capped at 100 MB heap (GitHub Advisory, Fix PR). Impact Successful exploitation causes the targeted Node.js process to exhaust available heap memory and crash with a fatal out-of-memory error, resulting in a complete availability loss for any service running on that process. There is no confidentiality or integrity impact — the vulnerability is purely a DoS vector. Applications most at risk are those that accept user-supplied URLs and pass them to Axios without filtering the data: scheme, such as link-preview services, URL proxies, or any backend that forwards user-provided URLs to Axios on Node.js (GitHub Advisory).
